originality.rationale: Substantive comparison, not timestamp: Hibi et al. (1412.3881) proves im<=reg<=min-match and studies dominating-induced-matching graphs — bounds/structural cases only, no uniform 986-row Betti census or dmax. Nguyen-Vu (1506.05769) classifies linearity defect<=1 as weakly chordal with im<=2 plus cycle formulas — family formula, not per-graph census with gap certificates. Matsuda-Yoshida (2112.15297) determines realizable (ind-match,min-match,match,n) and (reg,min-match,match,n) tuples — range theorem, not explicit per-graph tables/pruning replay or max(reg-im) witness. No fetched source publishes the 853-graph 7-vertex Betti census, the 286-table count, or dmax=1 with 48 attainers. Internal SCOPE049 covers only the 112 six-vertex graphs (plus frozen 8-graph 7-vertex sample, not complete); the 7-vertex complete census, 5-vertex stratum, and full-scope dmax are material new computation beyond it. Overlap on the 6-vertex stratum does not erase novelty of the headline full-scope gap maximum and 7-vertex census.

value.rationale: Headline is a rigorously established exact invariant of a natural closed object: max(reg(S/I(G))-im(G))=1 over all connected 5-7-vertex graphs, with full reg distributions, 286-table count, sandwich verification, and explicit extremal witness G*. Object and invariant were motivated before computation (Herzog-Hibi-Zheng / Katzman / Woodroofe regularity-vs-matching program); value (dmax, per-graph gaps, witness table) was not known or mechanically implied by bounds/family formulas/range theorems; a future conjecture-testing or characteristic-independence researcher could reasonably need the precise distributions and witness. Not a textbook restatement, parameter substitution, or unexplained number: gap quantifies non-tightness of im<=reg, witness (2,1) vs reg-3 graphs (gap 0) is interpretable. Complete 986-row census needs no general theorem per the exact-invariant standard.
